summary:
ECORA is a data-driven agricultural decision-support solution developed by Team Hasad to improve agricultural land utilization and crop diversity in Madinah, Saudi Arabia.

The region faces challenges related to water scarcity, extreme temperatures, and dependence on date palm cultivation. Our solution analyzes environmental conditions to recommend suitable alternative crops and optimal planting seasons.

Using monthly NASA POWER climate data from 2020 to 2025, ISRIC SoilGrids, and the FAO ECOCROP database of 2,568 plant species, we developed a prototype that evaluates crop suitability based on temperature, soil characteristics, and growing seasons.

Our preliminary results identified 372 plants with positive suitability scores, including chickpeas (100%), quinoa (93.3%), and guar (80%).

ECORA aims to support sustainable crop rotation, improve agricultural land utilization throughout the year, reduce unnecessary water consumption, and strengthen food security through science-based agricultural decisions.
details:
Project Overview

ECORA is an agricultural decision-support system developed by Team Hasad to help farmers in Madinah, Saudi Arabia, make better use of their agricultural land throughout the year.

Our project addresses limited crop diversity, water scarcity, and the underutilization of agricultural land by identifying alternative crops that are compatible with local environmental conditions.

How It Works

ECORA combines historical climate data, soil characteristics, and crop-specific environmental requirements to evaluate agricultural suitability.

The system follows five main steps:

  1. Collect monthly climate data from NASA POWER for Madinah between 2020 and 2025.
  2. Analyze local soil characteristics using ISRIC SoilGrids, including soil pH, texture, and organic carbon.
  3. Compare environmental conditions with the requirements of 2,568 plant species from the FAO ECOCROP database.
  4. Calculate crop suitability scores and identify optimal planting periods using an adapted OpenCLIM ECOCROP model.
  5. Rank potential crops and provide recommendations to support agricultural planning and future crop rotation strategies.

Results

Our preliminary analysis evaluated 2,026 plant species and identified 372 with positive suitability scores, representing 18.4% of the evaluated plants.

Promising seasonal crops include:

  • Chickpeas: 100% suitability.
  • Quinoa: 93.3% suitability.
  • Guar: 80% suitability.

These scores represent modeled environmental compatibility rather than guaranteed agricultural productivity.

Tools and Technologies

  • Python and Google Colab
  • Pandas, NumPy, Xarray, and Matplotlib
  • Rasterio and PyProj
  • NASA POWER
  • ISRIC SoilGrids
  • FAO ECOCROP
  • OpenCLIM ECOCROP

Innovation

ECORA transforms historical climate observations and soil data into actionable agricultural recommendations. Rather than focusing exclusively on traditional crops, our approach explores thousands of plant species to identify alternative agricultural opportunities.

The system considers seasonal temperature variations, soil compatibility, crop growth duration, and differences between seasonal and perennial plants.

Expected Impact

  • Improve agricultural land utilization throughout the year.
  • Encourage crop diversification.
  • Support sustainable crop rotation and soil health.
  • Help farmers make informed planting decisions.
  • Support more efficient water management and regional food security.

Future Development

Our next steps include integrating detailed irrigation requirements, soil salinity, satellite-based agricultural land mapping, and crop rotation optimization.

We also aim to collaborate with local farmers to validate our recommendations through field experiments and measure their actual impact on crop productivity, water consumption, and soil health.

The current prototype provides preliminary environmental suitability assessments. Field validation is necessary before implementing recommendations commercially.
